title: Research Readback V1 (what GET /api/projects/<id>/research answers)
$comment: Written against two payloads the product really emitted on 2026-10-22 -- a project holding one live finding plus one it superseded, and a project nobody filed anything for -- captured through design_lab.http_service.make_server on a live socket; see design-lab/scripts/verify_route_payload_contracts.py. Emitter: src/design_lab/research_review.py (readback). THE FINDINGS ARE REFERENCED, NOT RESTATED: every element of `findings` and every value of `current_findings` is the research finding itself, bound by design-lab/schemas/research-finding.schema.json, so a contract change moves into this file by reference instead of being restated and drifting. WHAT THIS SURFACE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT HAVE is a project-level verdict word. rights has `rights_clearance` because a rights gate exists; research has counts because writing findings down clears no gate, so `research_verdict` is bound to null and `proves_design_quality` / `is_knowledge_export` are bound to false below -- a future emitter that invents ACCEPTED or CLEARED here has to change this document, and that is the point. The gate vocabulary's own words must never appear in this body; design-lab/tests/test_research_http.py keeps asserting that against real responses.

superseded_finding_count.$comment: Kept apart from `current_finding_count`: a retired finding is evidence that work moved, not evidence that nothing was ever said.

unsourced_finding_count.$comment: Re-derived from the stored link rows, not read off the document. The finding contract requires at least one sourceRefs entry, so a positive number here means a row that predates or bypassed that rule -- which is why this is a count and not a constant.

source_ref_field.description: The field name the count was taken from, published so a reader can check the count against the rows.

unattributed_findings.$comment: Live findings whose author was never stated. The contract has no author field, so everything filed over HTTP appears here; a list rather than a count, because a count alone would let a page imply a person said each one.

undeclared_disclaimer.$comment: Live findings that never stated notDesignRule. Absence is legal in the contract and must not be read as a disclaimer, so the two cases are published separately.
